A Superseded Northern Settlement
This older proposal has been superseded by the existing Zoutpansberg administration. No new state or territorial transfer is required.

The northern settlement established by Potgieter in 1848 has become a centre of the existing Zoutpansberg community. Trade with Portuguese merchants and regional ivory routes supports its development. This event develops the town without founding a second republic.

In 1854 violence around the Nyl River escalated into a Boer commando siege of the caves at Makapansgat. Many African people died in the siege. Piet Potgieter was also killed, and Stephanus Schoeman succeeded him as commandant of Zoutpansberg. The succession belongs to our existing northern community, not to a new republic.
One Zoutpansberg Administration

An obsolete territorial settlement has duplicated the northern republic. Its Transvaal districts will return to the South African Republic, while districts already claimed by the existing Zoutpansberg administration will return to that administration. The established northern republic retains its own history and institutions.
Restore the existing administrations.
Lydenburg Joins Utrecht

The eastern burgher communities have agreed to conduct their common affairs through the Utrecht republic. The Lydenburg raad brings its districts into the united administration, while negotiations with the South African Republic continue. Local officers retain responsibility for their farms and settlements under the common government.
Unite the eastern districts under Utrecht.
Retain our separate government.
The Utrecht Republic Joins the South African Republic

The 1860 union brings the Republic of Utrecht, including the former Lydenburg districts, into the South African Republic. Zoutpansberg remains a distinct but associated republic under the SAR until the crisis of 1862.
Complete the union and continue as the South African Republic.
Zoutpansberg and the South African Republic
The Zoutpansberg community accepts association with the South African Republic while retaining its own government. This compact lasts until the crisis of 1862.
Northern Republican Calendar
Historical union dates are being coordinated.
Lydenburg Joins the South African Republic

The Utrecht negotiations have not established a common government. The Lydenburg raad must now consider a direct agreement with Pretoria, bringing its districts and public administration into the South African Republic.
Lydenburg and Its Capital

The eastern community has been represented by the Nelspruit district, while the town of Lydenburg remained under the western Boer administration. The town district will now join the existing Lydenburg community and become its capital. This settlement concerns the Lydenburg district alone and does not transfer Barberton or any land held by African or foreign states.
Seat the eastern raad at Lydenburg.
Accept SAR protection while retaining our republic.
